rules.sentence: Anterior interosseous nerve syndrome refers to an isolated palsy affecting these 3 muscles, without any associated sensory loss.
The condition typically presents with forearm pain and a distinctive weakness in the pincer movement of the index finger and thumb.

Clinicians should note that direct external trauma to the anterior interosseous nerve, which can produce similar muscle weakness, does not qualify as true anterior interosseous nerve syndrome due to its distinct pathophysiological mechanism.[3]
Most cases resolve spontaneously, and conservative management, including symptomatic treatment over a period of 3 to 6 months, remains the preferred initial strategy.[3]
